audit: Researched by a Sonnet child, then audited by the parent against s3. Film order matches s3's timestamps, with its 40 beats merged or dropped to 26. Six beats whose own notes admit a guess were downgraded to inferred (films 1, 3, 14, 18, 19, 20). s3 does not label a layer beat by beat, so the layer of each beat is a reading of what s3 and s1 describe.

sources.title: The Prestige (film), Wikipedia (plot is given in chronological order)
The Unreliable Diaries, The Prestige (fan analysis)
40 Beats (The Prestige), film-order beat list with timestamps
How The Prestige is written like its own magic trick, No Film School

not_fetched: The fandom wiki, a screenplay or transcript site and the Strange Horizons essay were not fetched this run, and the last 7,342 characters of the Wikipedia page were not read.

layers.name: Prison frame
layers.holder: Borden, awaiting the gallows, with Cutter's narration over the top
layers.text: Angier's Colorado diary reaches him through Lord Caldlow's solicitor; the trial, Caldlow's identity and the hanging also play here
layers.note: The novel's modern-day frame was replaced by Borden waiting to hang; Cutter's voice opens and closes the film.

layers.name: Angier's diary
layers.holder: Borden, reading it in his cell
layers.text: Angier's account of going to Colorado Springs to find Tesla, the machine and the London shows
layers.note: Per s2 it leaves out that the machine duplicates and the nightly drownings, so it works as a taunt aimed at Borden. Wikipedia does not name this diary.

layers.name: Borden's coded notebook
layers.text: Borden's account of the young years, the rivalry and the Transported Man, written in a cipher
layers.note: Olivia passes it to Angier; its keyword is Tesla, which is how it is read.

beats.what: Cutter explains a trick's three parts over Angier's final show
beats.note: Film order from s3. Story slot is a guess: the night Angier dies, after the nightly run began.

beats.what: In prison, Borden is offered Angier's diary in return for care of his daughter
beats.note: Film order from s3. Story slot after the trial is from s1's order.

beats.what: Angier arrives in Colorado Springs seeking Tesla and starts reading Borden's notebook
beats.note: Story slot is a guess from s1: Angier travels after he has the notebook and Fallon is kidnapped.

beats.what: Young Borden, Angier and Cutter work for Milton; bullet catch argument
beats.note: Earliest story event. s1 begins the chronology with the three working for Cutter and Julia's death; s3 gives this earlier scene.

beats.what: Cutter sends the pair to see Chung Ling Soo; Angier cannot lift the fishbowl
Julia drowns during a water-tank escape after a knot dispute
beats.note: s1 also puts Julia's drowning first in story order.

beats.what: At Julia's grave Angier asks which knot Borden tied
Borden marries Sarah and starts out with Fallon; Angier becomes the Great Danton
Angier sabotages Borden's bullet catch and Borden loses two fingers
Cutter builds Angier's bird act and brings in Olivia; Angier sees a Tesla demonstration
Borden debuts The Transported Man; Angier refuses to accept it uses a double
Angier hires lookalike Root and suffers hiding under the stage
Olivia spies on Borden, falls for him, and passes Angier the coded notebook
beats.note: Merges two s3 beats (spying, then the notebook handover); s1 agrees she passes the notebook.

beats.what: Borden buries Angier in a coffin; Cutter begs Angier to stop
beats.note: Story slot is a guess: s1 does not mention the coffin; placed just before Angier leaves for Colorado.

beats.what: Tesla warns Angier; the notebook's own text reveals Tesla was only the keyword
beats.note: Depth 2 because the text reads as the notebook; the scene is set in Colorado.

beats.what: The machine duplicates a cat; Angier finds a field of duplicate hats
Tesla leaves a warning, burns his lab and leaves the machine with Angier
Sarah takes her own life; the twin who loved her arrives too late
beats.note: The layer is a guess: it could be the prison frame's present rather than Angier's diary.

beats.what: Angier ships the machine to London and plans The Real Transported Man
beats.note: Layer is a reading: Angier's diary is where Borden would learn of it. Story order from s1.

beats.what: Angier performs nightly; the original drowns while the copy appears in the balcony
beats.note: Same layer doubt as the previous beat.

beats.what: Borden goes backstage, watches Angier drown and is found over the body
Borden is convicted of murder and sentenced to hang
Borden sees Lord Caldlow with his daughter and recognises Angier; Angier tears up his note
beats.note: s1 gives the same reveal and the torn note.

beats.what: Cutter learns Angier faked his death; Borden is hanged
A Borden twin shoots Angier in the basement and explains the shared life
beats.note: s1 puts the shooter and the twin reveal in the same scene.

beats.what: Angier's dying confession, Borden reunites with Jess, tanks revealed, Cutter closes

traps.says: Borden's private journal, readable with the right keyword, apparently exposing how he does the Transported Man
traps.does: Per s2, the keyword opens only personal entries, not the method; it was meant as a dead end, though it also confirmed Angier's Tesla lead.

traps.says: An honest record of the search for Tesla and the machine
traps.does: Per s2, it leaves out that the machine makes a copy and the nightly drownings, so it works as a taunt: Borden dies without understanding the backstage mechanism.

traps.says: Each diary seems to give an answer
traps.does: Per s4, each layer supplies an apparent answer while adding more misdirection, so the viewer is always one step behind.

claims.what: Number of performances Angier's final run was scheduled for
Number of water tanks or bodies shown or stated
claims.note: s1 says rows of tanks; no source fetched gives a count.

claims.value: 1890s Victorian London; Colorado Springs for the Tesla scenes
claims.note: s1 gives a decade, not specific years.

claims.what: Nolan's phrase for the adaptation problem
claims.value: journals within journals and stories within stories
claims.note: From a Variety interview, as reported by Wikipedia.

conflicts: s2 calls Angier reading Borden's notebook the first nested layer and Borden reading Angier's diary the second, while s3's order shows Angier's Colorado scenes first inside the prison frame and Borden's London past inside that; this page follows s3.

s3 does not label a layer beat by beat, and the beats from Sarah's death to Angier's nightly shows could be the prison frame's present rather than Angier's diary; this page draws them in the diary and marks them as guesses.
s1 does not describe Angier's diary at all and says the modern-day frame was replaced by Borden awaiting the gallows; the diary layer rests on s2 and s3.
